WHEREAS the Institute is the sole provider of advanced cardiac care for a network of 16 hospitals in our region, serving nearly 2 million people across Eastern Ontario, ensuring patients and communities throughout the region have access to world-leading cardiac care close to home; and
WHEREAS the Institute performs more cardiac procedures than any other hospital in Ontario, reflecting its commitment to innovative models of care, including Acute Cardiac Triage Unit which redirects patients from emergency departments across Eastern Ontario reducing the burden on partner hospitals; and
WHEREAS the One Million Canadian Hearts initiative, which is empowering Canadians with heart health knowledge and enabling swift interventions that save lives, is building a prevention model that could change how health care is delivered.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Ottawa City Council:

sub_agendas_items.title: Advance Left Turn Signal, northbound Prince of Wales/Waterbridge

motions.motion_text:
THAT the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion as Temporary Traffic Calming expenditures are restricted during the municipal election blackout period, which begins 27 August 2026.
WHEREAS the only access points for motorists travelling northbound on Prince of Wales Drive to enter the community located west of Prince of Wales Drive, north of Strandherd Drive and south of Merivale Road, are left turns at Fairpark Drive, which is unsignalized, and at Waterbridge Drive and Crestway Drive, which are signalized intersections; and
WHEREAS neither of the signalized intersections have advance or protected left turn phases; and
WHEREAS several unquantifiable factors that contribute to safety cannot be expressed through a traffic count; and
WHEREAS residents have expressed concerns about safety and wait times completing the left turn from Prince of Wales Drive northbound onto Waterbridge Drive and onto Crestway Drive due to southbound traffic volumes and rates of speed at which vehicles are travelling; and
WHEREAS the intersection of Prince of Wales Drive and Waterbridge Drive is the first signalized opportunity for motorists traveling northbound on Prince of Wales Drive, after crossing Strandherd Drive, to access the community west of Prince of Wales; and
WHEREAS the conditions required for staff to exercise delegated authority to implement an advance left turn signal (Type 9) onto Waterbridge Drive from Prince of Wales Drive in the northbound direction, are not met, andWHEREAS 2026 Temporary Traffic Calming funds not committed to a project cannot be carried over to the next term of Council; and
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council approve that staff install an advance left turn signal (Type 9) for northbound traffic on Prince of Wales Drive turning left onto Waterbridge Drive; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Council approve the use of funding from the Ward 24’s 2026 Temporary Traffic Calming budget to complete this work, which will occur after the blackout period.

sub_agendas_items.title: Demolition Control Waiver for 339 Roosevelt Avenue and 344 Winston Avenue

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion due to desired timeline to begin construction following the necessary demolition of the current buildings at 339 Roosevelt Avenue and 344 Winston Avenue.
WHEREAS Uniform Developments is planning to start construction of the first phase of the development at 335 Roosevelt Avenue as early as November and the total project contains approximately 300 residential units over two buildings (13 and 14 storeys); and
WHEREAS Uniform has concurred to the conditions of the Site Plan Approval Report, approved June 11, 2026; and
WHERAS Uniform is in the process of satisfying all the post approval requirements, including providing site securities, before the Site Plan Agreement package can be prepared; and
WHEREAS the Site Plan approval permits demolition once all fees and securities have been provided; and
WHEREAS demolition of the existing residential use buildings is required to begin site preparation working towards the targeted construction start prior to winter; and
WHEREAS staff have no concerns relating to the demolition of the buildings at 339 Roosevelt Avenue and 344 Winston Avenue prior to the completion of all conditions under Site Plan Control; and
WHEREAS by waiving demolition control application, the City will not receive $6,200.48 (includes $1,274.64 Legal Fee + HST) which is the fee associated with a demolition control application.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council waive demolition control approval for the demolition of 339 Roosevelt Avenue and 344 Winston Avenue and allow the applicant to proceed directly to demolition permits without agreement as the appropriate conditions and interim landscaping conditions are covered within the Site Plan approval.

sub_agendas_items.title: Relief for residents affected by the July 1, August 10 and August 12 weather events

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion in order to provide timely information to residents impacted by the July 1, August 10 and August 12, 2026 extreme weather events with respect to the temporary suspension of certain interest and fee accounts.
WHEREAS the extreme weather events of July 1, August 10 and August 12, 2026, caused significant disruption, property damage, and financial hardship for residents across the city, impacting more than 6,500 properties; and
WHEREAS the City’s Revenue Services team has implemented temporary administrative measures to support affected residents, including the suspension of collection activities, a pause on interest accumulation and related late fees, enhanced customer service accommodations, and account-level notifications for impacted properties; and
WHEREAS these temporary measures were implemented pursuant to sections 5-8 of the Delegation of Authority By-law (No. 2025-69), which authorize actions to be taken in cases of emergency or special circumstances; and
WHEREAS Council authorization is required to continue to provide financial relief measures, including the suspension of interest and penalty charges and the waiver of certain fees for affected residents; and
WHEREAS Council wishes to provide temporary financial relief to residents impacted by the July 1, August 10 and August 12, 2026 extreme weather events while recovery efforts continue;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council approve the temporary suspension of the following interest and fees applicable to accounts associated with properties and residents identified by the City Treasurer, in consultation with the Emergency Coordination Centre, as having been impacted by the July 1, August 10 and August 12, 2026 extreme weather events, effective July 1, 2026 and continuing until September 30, 2026 (the “Relief Period”):
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff continue the temporary suspension of collection activities, notices, dunning, and related collection actions for the affected properties and residents during the Relief Period.

sub_agendas_items.title: Engagement of Meteorologist for Ottawa-specific Weather Events
Review of Existing Land-Use Permissions and Developing a Municipal Framework for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Centres

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion in order to ensure staff have the necessary direction to develop a clear and consistent approach to respond to companies seeking to advance projects in Ottawa, in light of the developing context around Canadian digital sovereignty.
WHEREAS the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and other data-intensive technologies is increasing demand for data centre infrastructure across Canada, requiring municipalities to consider land use impacts and the municipal and electrical infrastructure required by data centres; and
WHEREAS due to recent global economic and political uncertainty, it’s expected that there will be an increasing requirement for data sovereignty within Canada, leading to an increased need for data centres situated within our country’s borders; and
WHEREAS there is widespread community interest in the land use considerations associated with large-scale data centres including municipal water and sanitary servicing, noise and heat generation, electrical power consumption, storage of hazardous materials or other community impacts; and
WHEREAS senior level governments are expected to influence the governance of data centre construction and how to protect municipalities as the Province recently released its Data Centre Playbook and the Federal Government released an AI Strategy in June 2026 (AI for All); and
WHEREAS there are various sizes of data centres and they will bring increased tax revenues and play an integral role in the economic ecosystem for the City of Ottawa and Canada;  and
WHEREAS the Official Plan does not currently include policies relating to data centres, and the City’s zoning bylaw permits data centres only in industrial areas today;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Staff be directed to undertake a study and develop a framework for assessing data centres based on their size and impact, which will include strong environmental and industrial standards, give consideration to community benefits and may include an Official Plan and/or Zoning By-law amendments; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff inform their analysis by the policies and plans produced by upper level of governments and return to Council with a report in Q1 2027; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that until this framework is brought to Council, staff make all of Council aware of any application for a hyperscale data center to allow the City to use other tools as it necessary (including Interim Control Bylaws) to manage community impacts.

sub_agendas_items.title: Residential Protective Plumbing Program Eligibility Update

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion in order to provide timely information to residents impacted by the July 1, August 10 and August 12, 2026 extreme weather events who are taking steps to protect their homes against future flooding.
WHEREAS the extreme weather events of July 1, August 10 and August 12, 2026, caused significant disruption, property damage, and financial hardship for residents across the city, impacting more than 6,500 properties; and
WHEREAS the Residential Protective Plumbing Program helps residents protect their homes against future weather events by providing rebates for primary and secondary sump pumps with battery backups (amount varies based on whether or not a sump pit needs to be constructed); and
WHEREAS numerous homes in Ottawa have whole home backup generators installed, providing the same backup power as a battery;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Residential Protective Plumbing Program eligibility be expanded to include primary and secondary sump pumps where a whole home backup generator is installed, retroactive to July 1, 2026.

sub_agendas_items.title: Reducing Speed Limit on Greenbank Road

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion in order to accelerate action as soon as possible in the upcoming school year.
WHEREAS on August 6, 2026, a vehicle exited the commercial plaza opposite Knoxdale Public School, illegally crossed multiple lanes of Greenbank Road, traversed the raised median, mounted the curb, and crashed through the school's perimeter fence and into the front schoolyard used by students; and
WHEREAS no children were present in the schoolyard at the time of the collision; however, had the same incident occurred during the school year while students were using the yard, the consequences could have been catastrophic; and
WHEREAS following the incident, the Ward Councillor engaged with local parents, school administration, the Ottawa-Carleton District School Board (OCDSB), provincial representatives, and City staff regarding potential safety measures; and
WHEREAS as an immediate response, the OCDSB has undertaken repairs to the damaged fence and has installed protective concrete barriers, while continuing to assess any additional measures that may be warranted; and
WHEREAS residents and parents have expressed concerns regarding the manoeuvre required to exit the commercial plaza opposite the school and proceed southbound on Greenbank Road, and have anecdotally identified this movement as potentially high-risk; and
WHEREAS there is currently insufficient information regarding the extent to which that turning movement contributed to the August 6 collision, or whether it has been a significant factor in the historical collision record at this location; and
WHEREAS a community petition calling for additional safety measures at Knoxdale Public School has received more than 200 signatures; and
WHEREAS Knoxdale Public School is unique within the Ottawa-Carleton District School Board in that it contains a front-facing kindergarten play yard immediately adjacent to an arterial roadway posted at 60 km/h without a school-area speed reduction; and
WHEREAS comparable OCDSB elementary schools situated along major roadways are subject to lower speed limits or school-zone speed reductions; and
WHEREAS at the request of the Ward Councillor, Traffic Services staff assessed the Greenbank Road corridor adjacent to Knoxdale Public School and Sir Robert Borden High School using the framework developed for the City's forthcoming Speed Zone Policy Review and determined that the recommended speed limit for this corridor would be 50 km/h; and
WHEREAS Traffic Services staff have advised that additional investigation would be required before any consideration could be given to restricting turning movements from the commercial plaza opposite Knoxdale Public School, including a review of relevant planning approvals, site plan agreements, and collision history; and
WHEREAS staff do not have the required delegated authority to make speed limit changes outside of the Council-approved Speed Zone Policy, and other speed-related policies.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council approve reducing the posted speed limit on Greenbank Road between Harrison Street and Bellman Drive from 60 km/h to 50 km/h; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the corresponding signage changes be completed as soon as practicable and that any costs associated with the installation of new signage and implementation of the speed limit reduction be funded from existing Public Works operating budget.

sub_agendas_items.title: Traffic Safety Assessment at the intersection of Diamondview Road and March Road

motions.motion_text:
THAT the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion at the August 26 meeting of Council in order to provide staff with timely direction in light of the recent collision and heightened concerns regarding this location.
WHEREAS local residents have raised ongoing concerns regarding traffic safety and conditions at the intersection of Diamondview Road and March Road; and
WHEREAS the recent fatal collision on August 21, 2026 has heightened concerns among residents and demonstrated the urgency of reviewing the safety of the intersection; and
WHEREAS there may be a range of measures available to improve safety at the intersection, including short-term traffic-calming and traffic-control measures, enhanced lighting, improved pavement markings, larger or additional signage, and other appropriate traffic safety measures; and
WHEREAS longer-term solutions may include the installation of traffic signals, a roundabout, or another intersection treatment identified through an engineering assessment as the safest and most appropriate solution; and
WHEREAS the City has identified the intersection of Diamondview Road and March Road as an Intersection Control Measures project within the April 2026 Amended Development Charges Background Study;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT staff undertake a review of the intersection of Diamondview Road and March Road, including a traffic safety assessment and review of collision history, traffic volumes, sightlines, lighting, signage, pavement markings and other relevant conditions;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff identify potential short-term measures that could be implemented to improve safety at the intersection while longer-term solutions are assessed; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review includes timelines associated with longer-term intersection treatments, including traffic signals, an all-way stop, a roundabout or other measures identified through the assessment as appropriate; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff be directed to provide regular updates to the Ward 5 Councillor on this work.

sub_agendas_items.title: Inventory of private catch basins

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion in order to ensure that staff can proceed immediately to ensure the City is well equipped to effectively manage future severe weather events, protect residential properties, and clarify long-term asset management obligations.
WHEREAS on July 1, 2026, a historic, record-breaking 1-in-200-year rainstorm event occurred within the City of Ottawa, delivering up to 167 millimetres of rainfall causing widespread flash flooding and thousands of reported basement backups; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa is an amalgamated municipality comprised of eleven former municipalities, each of which historically maintained varying infrastructure standards and levels of service with regard to rear yard residential drainage infrastructure; and
WHEREAS following amalgamation, development and easement standards across the city were inconsistent; and
WHEREAS infrastructure ownership and maintenance responsibilities are typically tied to property ownership unless an easement agreement states otherwise; and
WHEREAS in many instances across the city, private property owners actually own the drainage infrastructure themselves, with their properties functioning as critical catch basins for the surrounding area; and
WHEREAS a multi-departmental drainage easement working group has further updated standards to limit major systems to the Right of Way, with minor systems connecting to City-owned infrastructure in the Right of Way; and
WHEREAS to effectively manage future severe weather events, protect residential properties, and clarify long-term asset management obligations, the City must distinguish between private drainage systems, systems constructed as part of formal development agreements, and municipal infrastructure;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council direct staff from Infrastructure and Water Services; Planning, Development and Building Services; and from Legal Services to collaborate on a proposed plan to develop an inventory of private catch basins without existing City easements and to report back to the Environment and Climate Change Committee by Q2 2027 with:

sub_agendas_items.title: Response to US Tariffs

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion to allow staff to engage the relevant expertise to minimize impacts to Ottawa’s local economy.
WHEREAS the United States has been carrying out an extended tariff campaign against Canadian businesses, including the 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods imposed on August 22, creating significant economic pressure on businesses across Canada and in the City of Ottawa; and
WHEREAS Ottawa is home to a diverse economic base that includes manufacturers, small and medium-sized businesses operating across many industries that sell goods and services to the US, and a high-tech sector that together employ thousands of residents and contribute substantially to the city’s quality of life and economic prosperity; and
WHEREAS these tariffs threaten the competitiveness, economic viability, and growth of Ottawa’s manufacturers, small businesses, and high-tech companies and other industries through increased costs, disrupted supply chains, and reduced market access; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa amended the Procurement Bylaw in 2025 to follow Federal and Provincial trade policy introducing the Interim Policy on Reciprocal Trade from the federal government and the Buy Ontario Act from the provincial government. The federal policy supports reciprocal procurement by limiting contract awards, where feasible, to companies from jurisdictions that have reciprocal trade agreements with Canada. In addition, the provincial Buy Ontario Act encourages the use of Ontario and Canadian supply chains in light-duty fleet vehicle procurements and infrastructure projects; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa continues to be a strong consumer of local products in 2025, spending approximately 96 per cent of its annual purchasing dollars on goods and services from the local community; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa is committed to protecting local jobs, fostering economic resilience, attracting and retaining investment and talent, and ensuring that municipal policies and practices support the long-term success of Ottawa’s business community; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa is committed to protecting local jobs, fostering economic resilience, attracting and retaining investment and talent, and ensuring that municipal policies and practices support the long-term success of Ottawa’s business community;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Procurement be directed to continue to advance a Canada-first procurement strategy where at all possible, and work to reduce barriers for Ottawa companies interested in doing business with the City of Ottawa ; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to look for infrastructure solutions to connect Ontario and Quebec freight networks efficiently to improve supply chains and help regional economies to thrive; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City collaborate with Ville de Gatineau, the federal and provincial governments to designate the Ottawa-Gatineau area as a single economic region by advocating for reduced interprovincial trade barriers, leveraging current efforts within the tourism, defence and cybersecurity, technology and cultural sectors, and identifying new areas of opportunity to advance shared economic objectives; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Ottawa Tourism be requested to leverage its destination marketing, major event and convention attraction, sport hosting, and destination development activities, and capitalize on recent strong visitor metrics, to drive increased visitation and visitor spending in support of the visitor economy; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Economic Development Services, along with Invest Ottawa and other economic development organizations, be directed to assess the challenges and opportunities Ottawa businesses face from tariffs, and that Invest Ottawa tailor its advisory services and existing supports to help connect companies with customers, markets, capital, talent and other resources abroad, increasing their visibility, supporting diversification and risk reduction, accelerating commercialization and path to market and revenue, and continuing to drive investment attraction, business expansion, R&D and job creation in Ottawa; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City relaunch its “Buy Local, Shop Canadian” marketing campaign to encourage Ottawa residents to buy local wherever possible, as an act of solidarity with Ottawa companies and workers facing the impacts of these tariffs; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City update its “Tariff Toolkit” on ottawa.ca, outlining resources available to businesses and how residents and business owners can help support Canadian and local producers and businesses as they adapt to new and expanded tariffs; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff be directed to take a comprehensive look at other potential options within the City of Ottawa’s jurisdiction to help affected local businesses and report back before next council; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT residents and businesses be encouraged to proudly display Canadian flags in their windows as a visible expression of community solidarity and national pride during this period.

Post-Flood Residential Resilience Support

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the July 1, 2026 extreme rainfall event caused significant flooding impacts across the City of Ottawa, including in Ward 7 and the Crystal Beach community; and
WHEREAS flooding may occur through a variety of pathways, including overland flow, sewer surcharge, groundwater infiltration, and private-side plumbing or drainage limitations; and
WHEREAS the most appropriate flood-mitigation measures vary from property to property depending on how flooding occurred and the characteristics of the home; and
WHEREAS residents may experience challenges identifying the appropriate expertise, services, and information required to assess flooding impacts and evaluate potential mitigation measures; and
WHEREAS Council has previously provided direction regarding flood-event response, flood-resilience review activities, fee relief measures, and the City's Compassionate Grant Program and Residential Protective Plumbing Program; and
WHEREAS Council would benefit from information regarding potential approaches to supporting residents in navigating property assessment and flood-mitigation decision-making;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct the General Manager, Infrastructure and Water Services, in consultation with relevant departments, to report back through the 2026 Rainfall Analysis on options to develop a private-property flood resilience toolkit that complements existing Council directions;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff engage relevant stakeholders and service providers to identify existing supports, and potential partnership opportunities; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff examine how existing residential flood-resilience programs and initiatives, including Rain Ready Ottawa and related homeowner-support measures could contribute to improving resident access to information, guidance, and support following flooding events; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff undertake a jurisdictional review of homeowner-support, technical-assistance and private-side flood-mitigation programs offered by comparable Canadian municipalities and assess their applicability to Ottawa.

sub_agendas_items.title: Anti-Human Trafficking Task Force Framework

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS human trafficking is a serious crime and violation of human rights that disproportionately affects women, girls, youth, Indigenous peoples, newcomers, members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community, and other vulnerable populations; and
WHEREAS Statistics Canada data indicates that 416 police-reported human trafficking incidents were recorded in the Ottawa Census Metropolitan Area between 2014 and 2024, representing approximately 8.2 per cent of all police-reported incidents in Canada during that period, with Ottawa experiencing a rate significantly higher than the national average; and
WHEREAS the Ottawa Police Service Human Trafficking Unit reviewed 266 reports for possible human trafficking between January 1, 2023, and July 24, 2026, resulting in numerous criminal charges, demonstrating the continued prevalence of trafficking in Ottawa; and
WHEREAS Ontario's Anti-Human Trafficking Strategy 2025-2030 identifies prevention, early intervention, survivor supports, Indigenous-led approaches and enhanced coordination among partners as key priorities and includes a provincial investment of more than $345 million to combat human trafficking; and
WHEREAS numerous organizations in Ottawa currently provide critical services, supports, prevention programs, victim assistance, law enforcement, health, housing, education and community-based interventions related to human trafficking; and
WHEREAS there is an opportunity for the City of Ottawa to strengthen coordination, identify system gaps, improve information sharing, enhance prevention efforts and develop measurable community-wide objectives without duplicating the work of existing service providers and agencies;
WHEREAS in 2026, City Council approved Ottawa's refreshed2021 to 2031 Community Safety and Well-Being (CSWB) Plan, with a priority on gender based violence and violence against women. The plan sets out how the City works with community partners to improve the safety, health and well-being of Ottawa residents;
WHEREAS the as part of the CSWB Plan, the City has funded local community agencies to develop a community-led three-year Gender-based and Intimate Partner Violence Reduction Action plan (GBV-VAW Action Plan), informed by extensive sector engagement.
WHEREAS  A New Day Youth and Adult Services, and other Ottawa-based organizations contribute outstanding efforts to supporting survivors of human trafficking and sexual exploitation through trauma-informed care, long-term housing, counselling, and individualized recovery programs.
WHEREAS through its survivor-centered approach, A New Day empowers young people to heal, rebuild their lives, and move toward independence with dignity, hope, and community support.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Community and Social Services (CSSD) work with A New Day, and other organizations contributing to a GBV-VAW Action Plan, under the CSWB Plan, to create a Human Trafficking Task Force as a multi-sector, survivor-informed advisory body with the objective of improving community coordination, prevention, accountability and system-level responses to human trafficking in Ottawa to be announced in Q4 of 2026; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Task Force shall not duplicate the operational mandates of existing service providers, law enforcement agencies, community tables, or provincial programs, but shall instead focus on strategic coordination, policy advice, systems planning, advocacy to all levels of government and public education and awareness; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the appointed Task Force will develop the final structure, terms of reference, membership composition and governance model for the Task Force.

sub_agendas_items.title: OCC-2026-19 - Catch basin design and maintenance
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by L. Johnson
Following the July 1, 2026 flooding of thousands of west end Ottawa homes, businesses, and public facilities, and again after the flooding on August 10, 2026, many residents noted that stormwater drainage through municipal catch basins was inhibited by Inlet Control Devices (ICDs) which had been installed by the City.
Several also noted that the ICDs were plugged with dirt and debris, completely blocking the catch basin from draining storm water.
The apparent result of the ICDs, whether blocked or not, was to cause overland flooding that entered homes.

sub_agendas_items.title: OCC-2026-20 - Next Steps for a Health Hub Development
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by S. Desroches
There are several municipally-owned properties in the northern part of Findlay Creek that are expected to become surplus in the coming years, including the former Gloucester City Hall, Leitrim Police Station and public works yard.
These properties becoming surplus presents an opportunity for the community to explore potential uses of these lands to better serve the area, including a health hub.
I have routinely heard from residents that having more healthcare opportunities closer to home is very important.
This plan also aligns with the City’s Primary Care Provider Recruitment and Retention Strategy aiming to ensure more Ottawa residents have access to a family doctor or nurse practitioner.
